Subject: Follow-up: trace field handoff + SDK auth & routing for NimbleHealth POC

Hi Jason / Priya —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and clearly defined next steps so we can align engineering workstreams for the POC. I tried to keep this tight — please flag anything missing.

What we agreed on (high level):
- Goal: Validate a latency < 220ms p50 for user-facing completion calls and an embeddings/rerank flow that meets our 200ms target for short lists.
- Integration surface: SDK (Node + Python), server-to-server calls from your ingestion pipeline, and a lightweight client-side call for tool-calling UI events.

Key integration items (owner / target):
1) SDK + auth: Redwood SDK will support API key short-lived tokens for the UI path and mTLS for server-to-server (recommended for ingestion). Action: Rishi to share code snippets and token-refresh example. (Owner: Rishi — ETA: 2027-04-23)
2) Routing & fallbacks: Primary routing to us-east-1, fallback eu-west-1 for capacity/region failover. Also discussed model-variant fallback (gpt-medium -> gpt-small) for graceful degradation. Action: Olga to share routing policy example for your infra. (Owner: Olga — ETA: 2027-04-23)
3) Structured output & tool-calling: We'll provide a function-calling schema for the ‘payment_lookup’ and ‘patient_summary’ calls. Action: Priya to share expected schema; Redwood will return JSON + signature fields. (Owner: Priya / Redwood — ETA: 2027-04-25)
4) Embeddings & reranker: We suggested using dense embeddings for candidate prefiltering followed by Redwood reranker model for final ordering. Action: supply a test vector set (20–50 queries) and we'll run a quick quality sweep. (Owner: NimbleHealth — ETA: 2027-04-28)
5) Observability hooks (critical): We need the following to arrive in each request/response:
   - trace_id (x-rw-trace-id) propagated from your frontend through any proxies to Redwood
   - session_id and user_id logging fields (used to join with your analytics)
   - latency headers we expose: x-rw-latency-total, x-rw-latency-model, x-rw-latency-proxy (for fine-grained dashboards)
   - request_type tag (completion | embeddings | rerank) to drive per-route dashboards
   Action: Jason to confirm your front-end can attach x-rw-trace-id and preserve it through your API gateway. (Owner: Jason — ETA: 2027-04-22)

Attachments: I attached a one-page POC mutual-action-plan (20270422-nimble-poc-mpa.xlsx) and the scope doc (nimble_poc_scope.pdf). Link to shared Drive with templates is below.

Next steps and invites:
- Rishi + Jason: sync on SDK auth model and sample token refresh (30 min) — can we do Tues 4/23 9am PT?
- Technical POC kickoff (90 min) with engineering + security (proposed Thurs 4/25) — Olga to send calendar invite after we confirm times.

If that all looks right I’ll open the POC workspace and provision test keys.

Thanks —
Olga Petrov

Thanks Olga — high level looks good. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 

1) Latency targets: p50 220ms is doable for the UI flow if model variant stays within our compute budget — can you confirm what model you expect us to run for the initial POC (gpt-medium-2048)? Also want to make sure prefix cache options are available for repeated patient prompts.

2) Trace propagation: Our front-end uses an in-house request-id header (x-nh-req). We can surface x-rw-trace-id but we need to know whether Redwood will accept x-nh-req as an alias or require you to map it.

3) Auth: mTLS for ingestors is fine. For short-lived UI tokens we prefer OAuth-style flows vs raw API keys. Do you have a refresh-token example?

We can do the Rishi sync Tues 4/23 9am PT. Priya will follow up with a small test vector set by Friday.

Hi all — quick engineering notes ahead of our sync (I’ll bring code samples to the call):

- SDK / auth: we support three auth modes for the POC:
  1) short-lived API keys (recommended for client-initiated calls) with token-refresh endpoint (example: POST /v1/auth/refresh -> returns ephemeral key TTL 15m)
  2) OAuth bearer (we can federate with your IdP if you want)
  3) mTLS for server-to-server ingestion (mutual TLS certs and CN mapping)
  Example Node init snippet I’ll share on the call; Python is nearly identical.

- Headers & trace mapping: Redwood will read x-rw-trace-id first. We also accept custom aliases via a header mapping config (x-trace-alias: x-nh-req) — that mapping is configured at the POC workspace level (we can enable for NimbleHealth). For logging fields we recommend sending: x-rw-trace-id, x-rw-session-id, x-nh-user-id (we’ll map to user_id).

- Caching: prefix/KV caching is supported; best practice for patient-facing prompts is to use a short-term prefix cache (TTL 2–5m) plus the reranker for candidate freshness.

- Latency headers we emit (example):
  x-rw-latency-total: 185ms
  x-rw-latency-model: 120ms
  x-rw-latency-proxy: 40ms
  x-rw-cache-hit: true|false

I’ll prepare a minimal curl + SDK snippet to demonstrate header propagation and token refresh before the call.

See you Tues 9am PT.
Rishi
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
